title: Replicating Alignment Faking Under Multiple Operator Identity Framings

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: distinguishes whether alignment faking is a prompted artifact (sensitive to framing) or a deep strategic behavior (persists regardless). This directly informs how seriously the alignment community should treat alignment faking findings.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: inference-only experiment. Vary system prompt framings (3 conditions) and measure compliance rates. No training or adversarial optimization needed. 8B models are within medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: 3 system prompt framings on 1-2 models, measuring differential compliance rates. Simple, well-defined experimental design directly adapted from published protocol.

novelty.reasoning: The original alignment faking paper (Greenblatt et al., Dec 2024) used Anthropic-specific framing. Anthropic's 'Alignment Faking Revisited' (2025) found that 'small variations in the prompt that prior to RL had no substantial effect on the compliance gap — such as swapping the AI company from Anthropic to OpenAI — now greatly increase the compliance gap.' This directly addresses the operator identity framing question. Koorndijk (2025) and the LessWrong replication also explored prompt sensitivity. The specific finding that operator identity framing matters has been documented, though a systematic study across multiple framings (3+ conditions) on open-weight models adds incremental value.

evidence: Greenblatt et al. Alignment faking in large language models. arXiv:2412.14093, Dec 2024.
